This notebook accompanies the full report on survival for 50 years after graduation among University of Adelaide graduates.

It follows the analysis from exploratory plots to model selection, with the original R code throughout.

# Data and exploration

*Companion to report Sections 2-3.*

## Import and inspect the data

The data record survival counts for graduates from 1938-1947, grouped by faculty, sex and graduation year.

Faculty codes denote arts (A), engineering (E), medicine (M) and science (S).


```{r}
data = read.csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/richardpmann/richardpmann.github.io/refs/heads/main/MATH3823/Datasets/adelaide-48.csv')
attach(data)
as.factor(faculty)
as.factor(sex)
summary(data)
```

## Compare observed survival rates

These boxplots compare the proportion surviving for 50 years after graduation across faculties, sexes and graduation years.

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1,3))
# EDA
boxplot(survive/total ~ faculty, xlab = 'Faculty', ylab = 'Survival Probability', main = 'Survival Probability by Faculty')
boxplot(survive/total ~ sex, xlab = "Sex", ylab = "Survival Probability", main = "Survival Probability by Sex")
boxplot(survive/total ~ year, xlab = "Year", ylab = "Survival Probability", main = "Survival Probability by Year")
```

## Inspect the overall distribution

The histogram shows how observed survival proportions vary across the recorded groups.

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1,1))
hist(survive/total, main = 'Histogram of Chances of Survival', xlab = 'Survival Rate', breaks = 10)
```

# Baseline model

*Companion to report Sections 4-5.*

## Fit the full binomial model

The initial model includes graduation year, faculty and sex, using a logit link.

The summaries and diagnostic plots provide a starting point for model comparison.

```{r}
# Question 1
model1 = glm(
  cbind(survive, total - survive) ~ year + faculty + sex,
  family = binomial
)
summary(model1)

anova(model1)

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(model1, which = 1:2, main = 'Model 1')
```

## Predict survival for two graduate profiles

The model estimates survival probabilities and standard errors for two example profiles.

The female engineering profile has no direct observations in the dataset, so its prediction relies on the model's assumptions.

```{r}

ex_data1 = data.frame(sex = c('M', 'F'), year = c(1941, 1938), faculty = c('M', 'E'))
ex_data_fit = predict.glm(model1, ex_data1, type = 'response', se.fit = T)$fit
ex_data_se = predict.glm(model1, ex_data1, type = 'response', se.fit = T)$se.fit
cat("Fitted Values:\n", ex_data_fit, "\n", 
    "Standard Errors:\n", ex_data_se, "\n")
```

# Model selection

*Companion to report Section 5.1.*

## Remove graduation year

Model 2 retains faculty and sex, testing whether graduation year adds useful explanatory power.

The likelihood ratio test, AIC and diagnostic plots support comparison with the full model.

```{r}
# Simplifying model
model2 = glm(
  cbind(survive, total - survive) ~  faculty + sex,
  family = binomial
)
summary(model2)
anova(model2)
anova(model2, model1, test = 'Chisq')
AIC(model2, model1)
cat(" Deviance of model1: ", deviance(model1), "\n",
    "Deviance of model2: ", deviance(model2), "\n",
    "AIC of model1: ", AIC(model1), "\n",
    "AIC of model2: ", AIC(model2), "\n")
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(model2, which = 1:2, main = 'Model 2')
```

## Combine medicine and arts

Model 3 groups medicine and arts as MA, reducing the number of faculty parameters.

The comparison checks whether this simplification materially worsens model fit.

```{r}
# Generate a combine M and A factor levels into MA
faculty2 = faculty
faculty2[faculty2 == 'M'] = 'MA'
faculty2[faculty2 == 'A'] = 'MA'
faculty2 = as.factor(faculty2)

model3 = glm(cbind(survive, total - survive) ~ faculty2 + sex,
             family = binomial
)
summary(model3)
anova(model3, model2, test = 'Chisq')
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(model2, which = 1:2, main = 'Model 2')
plot(model3, which = 1:2, main = 'Model 3')
```

## Combine science and engineering

Model 4 also groups science and engineering as SE, leaving two faculty groups alongside sex.

The report selects this model as its preferred balance of fit and simplicity for the combined data.

```{r}
faculty3 = faculty
faculty3[faculty3 == 'M'] = 'MA'
faculty3[faculty3 == 'A'] = 'MA'
faculty3[faculty3 == 'S'] = 'SE'
faculty3[faculty3 == 'E'] = 'SE'
faculty3 = as.factor(faculty3)

model4 = glm(cbind(survive, total - survive) ~ faculty3 + sex,
                 family = binomial
)
summary(model4)
anova(model4, model3, test = 'Chisq')
anova(model4, model1, test = 'Chisq')
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(model3, which = 1:2, main = 'Model 3')
plot(model4, which = 1:2, main = 'Model 4')
```

# Further comparisons

*Further checks from report Sections 5.2-5.3.*

## Test a faculty-sex interaction

Model 5 tests whether the association between faculty group and survival differs by sex.

```{r}

model5 = glm(cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ faculty3 * sex,
             family = binomial
)

summary(model5)
anova(model4, model5, test = 'Chisq')
```

## Test interactions with graduation year

These tests assess whether the year association differs by sex or faculty group, compared with a model retaining all three main effects.

```{r}
year_baseline = glm(cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ faculty3 + sex + year,
                    family = binomial)
sex_year_model = glm(cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ faculty3 + sex*year,
                     family = binomial)
faculty_year_model = glm(cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ faculty3*year + sex,
                         family = binomial)
anova(year_baseline, sex_year_model, test = 'Chisq')
anova(year_baseline, faculty_year_model, test = 'Chisq')
```

## Group graduation years around the war

This model compares pre-war, wartime and post-war graduation groups while retaining faculty group and sex.

The accompanying boxplot shows the observed survival proportions in each period.

AIC compares this model with the original linear-year model, these two models are not nested.

```{r}
pre_post_war = cut(year, breaks = c(1930, 1939, 1945, 2000), labels = c("Pre-War", "During-War", "Post-War"))
pre_post_war = as.factor(pre_post_war)

war_model = glm(cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ pre_post_war + faculty3 + sex,
                family = binomial)
summary(war_model)
anova(model4, war_model, test = 'Chisq')
AIC(model1, war_model)


par(mfrow = c(1,1))
boxplot(survive/total ~ pre_post_war, xlab = '', ylab = 'Survival Probability', main = 'Survival Probability by Pre/During/Post War')

```

## Compare graduation before and from 1940

A second time grouping compares graduation before 1940 with graduation in 1940 or later.

The likelihood ratio test checks whether this split improves on Model 4.

```{r}
decade_split = cut(year, breaks = c(1930, 1939, 2000), labels = c("Pre-1940", "Post-1940"))
decade_split = as.factor(decade_split)

decade_model = glm(cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ decade_split + faculty3 + sex,
                family = binomial)
summary(decade_model)
anova(model4, decade_model, test = 'Chisq')
```

# Analysis by sex

The following models examine faculty and graduation year separately for male and female graduates.

## Prepare the subsets

The data are split by sex, with separate variable names for each subset.

```{r}

male_data = data[data$sex == "M", ]
female_data = data[data$sex == "F", ]
colnames(male_data) <- paste0(colnames(male_data), "_M")
colnames(female_data) <- paste0(colnames(female_data), "_F")
attach(male_data)
attach(female_data)
as.factor(faculty_M)
as.factor(faculty_F)




faculty3_F = faculty_F
faculty3_F[faculty3_F %in% c('M', 'A')] = "MA"
faculty3_F[faculty3_F %in% c('S', 'E')] = "SE"
```

## Male graduates: assess graduation year

The first comparison tests whether graduation year improves a model containing faculty.

```{r}
male_model1 = glm(cbind(survive_M, total_M-survive_M) ~ faculty_M + year_M,
                 family = binomial
)

summary(male_model1)
anova(male_model1)

male_model2 = glm(cbind(survive_M, total_M-survive_M) ~ faculty_M,
                  family = binomial
)
summary(male_model2)
anova(male_model2, male_model1, test = "Chisq")
```

## Male graduates: combine medicine and arts

The next model groups medicine and arts, then compares the fit with separate faculty levels.

```{r}
faculty2_M = faculty_M
faculty2_M[faculty2_M %in% c('M', 'A')] = 'MA'
faculty2_M = as.factor(faculty2_M)

male_model3 = glm(cbind(survive_M, total_M-survive_M) ~ faculty2_M,
                  family = binomial
)
summary(male_model3)
anova(male_model3, male_model2, test = "Chisq")
```

## Male graduates: retain two faculty groups

Science and engineering are also combined, giving the report's preferred model for male graduates.

```{r}
faculty3_M = faculty_M
faculty3_M[faculty3_M %in% c('M', 'A')] = "MA"
faculty3_M[faculty3_M %in% c('S', 'E')] = "SE"
faculty3_M = as.factor(faculty3_M)
male_model4 = glm(cbind(survive_M, total_M-survive_M) ~ faculty3_M,
                                family = binomial
)
summary(male_model4)
anova(male_model4, male_model3, test = "Chisq")
```

## Female graduates: compare simpler models

These comparisons assess models with faculty and year, faculty alone, and an intercept only.

The report finds insufficient evidence at the 5% level to prefer the predictors over the intercept-only model.

```{r}
female_model1 = glm(cbind(survive_F, total_F-survive_F) ~ faculty_F + year_F,
                    family = binomial
)
summary(female_model1)
anova(female_model1)

female_model2 = glm(cbind(survive_F, total_F-survive_F) ~ faculty_F,
                    family = binomial
)
summary(female_model2)
anova(female_model2, female_model1, test = "Chisq")

female_model3 = glm(cbind(survive_F, total_F-survive_F) ~ 1,
                    family = binomial
)
summary(female_model3)
anova(female_model3, female_model2, test = "Chisq")
anova(female_model3, female_model1, test = "Chisq")
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(female_model3)
```

## Compare the observed patterns by sex

The final plots compare faculty and year patterns using a shared survival-rate scale.

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
boxplot(survive_M/total_M ~ faculty_M, xlab = 'Faculty', ylab = 'Survival Probability', main = 'Survival Probability by Faculty (Male)', ylim = c(min(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE), max(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE)), col = 'turquoise')
boxplot(survive_F/total_F ~ faculty_F, xlab = 'Faculty', ylab = 'Survival Probability', main = 'Survival Probability by Faculty (Female)', ylim = c(min(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE), max(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE)), col = 'pink')
boxplot(survive_M/total_M ~ year_M, xlab = "Year", ylab = "Survival Probability", main = "Survival Probability by Year (Male)", ylim = c(min(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE), max(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE)), col = 'turquoise')
boxplot(survive_F/total_F ~ year_F, xlab = "Year", ylab = "Survival Probability", main = "Survival Probability by Year (Female)", ylim = c(min(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE), max(data$survive/data$total, na.rm = TRUE)), col = 'pink')
```

See the report for the statistical reasoning, detailed results and interpretation.
